PullRequest.Title: sessions: Preserve remote hosts after tunnel discovery failures
PullRequest.Body:
## What is changing

Tunnel discovery failures no longer look like an authoritative empty inventory in the Agents Window. Cached remote hosts remain available when browser authentication or enumeration fails, while a successful empty discovery can still remove hosts that no longer exist.

Deleting a tunnel now updates the picker as soon as deletion succeeds. If the follow-up refresh fails, the deleted tunnel stays removed and the error explains that refresh—not deletion—failed.

Before:
- A transient discovery failure could remove cached remote hosts.
- A successful deletion followed by a failed refresh reported that deletion failed and left the deleted tunnel visible.

After:
- Discovery failures preserve cached hosts; only successful discovery reconciles the cache.
- Successful deletion removes the tunnel immediately, keeps other picker entries available, and reports refresh failure separately.

## How it is changing

The browser tunnel services propagate authentication and enumeration failures to the reconciliation layer instead of returning an empty list. The shared tunnel contribution preserves its prior cache when discovery rejects. Direct service tests cover both browser implementations, and web tunnel lifecycle logs include connection timing and browser connectivity context for diagnosis.

## Manual validation

In an isolated Code OSS Agents Window built from this branch, a scripted tunnel deletion succeeded and the subsequent refresh failed. The picker stayed open, removed only the deleted tunnel, retained the other tunnel, and displayed the distinct refresh-failure notification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Startup, focus, session-change, and manual rediscovery of cached dev tunnels
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A silent status check must obtain authentication and complete one tunnel inventory request before reconciliation updates cached providers and statuses; automatic connection attempts are independent and may proceed concurrently from already-cached entries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate the account's dev tunnels through the browser SDK or embedder discovery provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory request per status-check trigger, independent of tunnel count; successful results are reconciled in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request occurred; failures were converted to an empty inventory in these browser implementations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of status reconciliation, but does not block already-staged cached-host connection attempts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delegate desktop tunnel enumeration to the shared process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per authenticated status check; no request occurs when authentication is unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC request occurred when authenticated; missing authentication returned an empty inventory instead of rejecting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or restore a tunnel connection for cached entries when auto-connect is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight dial per cached address; independent addresses can dial concurrently, and failed nonterminal dials use the existing capped 10-attempt exponential retry policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cached entries were already auto-connected before discovery; a failed discovery was previously interpreted as empty and subsequently removed them, while the diff intentionally retains them and therefore also retains their bounded reconnect eligibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the discovery reconciliation critical path, but consumes background network resources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of cached tunnel addresses; discovery remains one grouped inventory request, while background connection work scales by cached address with per-address coalescing and capped retries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Status-check invocations are not globally coalesced, but the diff does not change that behavior. Connection dials are coalesced per address; different cached addresses can connect concurrently under the existing service policy.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful discovery still authoritatively reconciles the persisted cache, including successful empty results. Failed discovery now preserves the warm cache and providers. There is no added cache key or unbounded retention; entries remain bounded by the user's persisted tunnel inventory and later successful reconciliation or explicit removal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-request discovery cardinality, cache-preservation behavior, per-address dial coalescing, and retry cap from the traced implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may have multiple cached tunnels and prolonged network failures can retain bounded retry work, but typical cardinality and connection duration are unknown. The retained retries are coupled to the requested availability behavior and governed by existing caps.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Failure semantics change cache lifetime rather than adding successful-path boundary calls; retained connection attempts are bounded and are part of keeping cached hosts available.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Connect via Dev Tunnel picker and delete a tunnel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening waits for authentication and one inventory request. Deletion waits for confirmation and one delete request; after success the picker is updated locally before the existing refresh inventory request completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate tunnels when opening the picker and refreshing after deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list call on open and one list call after each confirmed successful deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial and post-delete list calls occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial listing blocks picker population; post-delete refresh keeps the picker busy, but the local removal is visible immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete the selected tunnel through the service or embedder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one delete call per confirmed item deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same delete call occurred before refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must succeed before the item is locally removed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tunnel inventory size controls local filtering, sorting, item allocation, and picker assignment. The diff adds one immediate O(N log N) picker rebuild per successful deletion before the existing refresh rebuild.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Deletion is serialized by the isDeleting guard; delete and refresh are sequential, with no added concurrent boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The tunnel service removes the deleted tunnel from persisted cache after successful deletion; the local picker array is also filtered immediately. A failed refresh preserves the remaining displayed entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the extra local rebuild and unchanged network cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tunnel lists are expected to be small; no evidence establishes a size where the extra user-triggered picker rebuild causes perceptible UI cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only added work is a bounded immediate in-memory picker update on a user-triggered deletion; expensive boundary count and ordering are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect, exchange protocol messages, reconnect, and close an embedder-provided web tunnel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial connect waits on one embedder connection call; each received JSON frame is parsed and synchronously forwarded to the protocol client. Reconnect waits on one embedder connection call per existing reconnect attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish the initial or replacement tunnel transport through the embedder discovery provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connect call for initial establishment and one per reconnect attempt; the diff only surrounds these calls with timing/context logs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider connect calls occurred with the same sequencing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks initial connection or reconnection completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse each inbound JSON frame and stringify each outbound protocol message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same JSON parse/stringify occurred; the diff adds one Date.now clock read per inbound frame and lifecycle-only logging.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Inbound protocol-frame rate and number of connection/reconnection lifecycle events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A transport processes each event callback synchronously. Reconnection scheduling and coalescing remain in the existing ReconnectingTransport and remote-host service; the diff does not alter them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved on the frame path. Timing fields retain three scalar values per live transport and are released with the transport.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in per-frame placement and constant retained state, with low confidence that its magnitude is material.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Protocol traffic rate varies, but a single clock read per frame is small relative to the existing JSON parse and event dispatch; no benchmark or call-path evidence indicates user-visible CPU or frame impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added diagnostics do not add network calls, unbounded retention, serialization, or materially expensive synchronous work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all nine changed files. Traced discovery/cache reconciliation, picker deletion, auto-connect/retry behavior, and web tunnel transport instrumentation. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and there was insufficient evidence that this PR fixes a shipped performance regression requiring blame attribution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
